questions.prompt: After git init in /tmp/git-lab, you have:
choices: A GitHub repository
A local repository (a .git directory). GitHub is a host, not Git
A remote named origin pointing at GitHub
Only a working tree; a repository starts when you push
questions.why: git init creates .git on disk. A GitHub page is a copy plus a UI. First success never leaves the laptop.

questions.prompt: You edited notes.txt and saved it in the editor. git commit with no add will:
choices: Commit the saved file because the editor already wrote it to disk
Commit only what is in the index; a saved unstaged file is not in the next snapshot
Commit every file under the directory
Create a branch named notes.txt
questions.why: The working tree is the desk; the index is the next snapshot. git add copies into the index. git commit writes a commit from the index.

choices: A saved diff Git reapplies later
A snapshot of the index plus parent, author, date, and message
A GitHub pull request
The contents of the working tree, including untracked files
questions.why: Git stores snapshots. It can show a diff between two commits. Untracked files are not in the index, so they are not in the commit.

choices: A special Git object type that other branches cannot have
A default branch name: a movable pointer at a commit
The remote named origin
Required before git init will work
questions.why: A branch is a name pointing at a commit. main/master is the default name, not a special object.

questions.prompt: git remote -v prints nothing. Which is true?
choices: origin still exists; Git always has GitHub as origin
This repo has no remote. origin is a name you add, not a default host
You must git clone again to get a remote
git init failed
questions.why: A remote is a URL or path Git knows how to fetch and push. After init the list is empty until git remote add.

questions.prompt: You already git cloned this learning guide. That means:
choices: You finished the Git first success
You copied an existing repo (and usually got origin). First success is still git init in /tmp/git-lab
GitHub Actions will run on your laptop
You must not run git init anywhere else
questions.why: Clone is a download plus a remote. First success is init, add, commit, log in a throwaway directory, not in the guide clone.

questions.prompt: You committed PASSWORD=demo in .env, then git rm'd the file and committed again. The password is:
choices: Gone from git; git rm deletes history
Still in the old commit. If that commit was pushed, rotate the password
Hidden by .gitignore, which rewrites old commits
Safe because /tmp repos cannot be cloned
questions.why: A later commit can drop the file from the tree. The old blob stays. .gitignore does not rewrite history. Rotate a pushed secret.
